summary: This class models a traffic light that starts on red and cycles red \u2192 green \u2192 yellow \u2192 red each time advance() is called, plus a method that reports whether traffic must stop. It is the subject under test for the badly written traffic light tests that follow.

lines.text: The light's colour is private, so tests can only observe it through getColor(), and the initial value fixes the starting state every new TrafficLight begins in.
Calling equals on the literal rather than on color is a deliberate habit: it can never throw a NullPointerException, however the field was set.
The chain of else-if branches is what makes advance() a cycle; each call moves exactly one step, so a test that expects green must first advance once from the starting red.
The final else quietly treats anything that is not red or green as yellow, which is why the whole cycle relies on the field never holding an unexpected value.
One negated comparison covers two stop colours, red and yellow, so a thorough test class needs a separate, clearly named test for each of them rather than a single catch-all assertion.
